transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-06-07 15:00 PDT | Duration 52 minutes | Recording available
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood CSM), Evan Torres (Portside Head of ML), Sofia Rivera (Infra Lead), Jordan Lee (Procurement), Priya Nandakumar (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick renewal check-in to discuss contract extension + capacity upgrade request for additional EU region, go/no-go on dedicated nodes versus hosted burst, security questions (SOC2, KMS), and next steps to run a short pilot and finalize commercial terms.

00:00 Maya Chen: Okay, hi everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me all right?
00:06 Evan Torres: Yeah loud and clear, thanks Maya.
00:09 Maya Chen: Great, I'll do a quick frame — today we wanted to review your upcoming renewal, the expansion ask for eu-west region, and the dedicated capacity options you mentioned over email. Ravi's on for any technical details, Lina for the CSM side.
00:23 Priya Nandakumar: Thanks, short agenda works. We're mainly focused on predictable throughput for Q4 and data residency in EU.
00:31 Maya Chen: Perfect. Evan, maybe can you start with current usage and what's driving the need for extra region?
00:36 Evan Torres: Sure. So we've been live with Redwood since Jan '26 for our customer support summarization and routing pipelines. Workload is spiky — we see 2x baseline during EMEA business hours and then weird peaks when batch jobs kick off. Most of the traffic currently hits us in us-east-1, latency's been fine but the EU customers want lower tail latency and also we need to ensure token residency for some EU accounts. So we're looking at deploying eu-west-1 nodes and ideally dedicated capacity for predictable SLAs.
01:12 Ravi Patel: Quick clarifying Q — when you say dedicated, are you thinking fully reserved GPU pools, or reserved baseline with burst into host?
01:18 Evan Torres: Baseline reserved with ability to burst would be ideal — we don't want to pay for idle capacity but also can't accept dropped requests during peak.
01:25 Sofia Rivera: And compliance note — some of our logistics partners require logs and audit trails to stay in-region, so we need to confirm audit log retention and KMS integration for keys stored in EU.
01:37 Lina Gomez: We can definitely route logs and set retention. Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM and audit export — I'll follow up with the exact retention windows.
01:45 Priya Nandakumar: On contract, we've got a renewal in July — our legal wants a firm term and some SLA guarantees, and we're evaluating adding a year plus a higher commit for discounted pricing if the EU region is included.
01:59 Jordan Lee: Procurement will also need a statement of work and a clear invoice schedule, plus PO details.
02:07 Maya Chen: Good context, thanks. Ravi, walk us through the performance side for dedicated pools and how we handle failover and fallback to hosted variants.
02:14 Ravi Patel: Sure. So Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools that we can provision in eu-west-1. You can choose baseline reserved vCPU/GPU capacity and a burst pool that uses our hosted fleet if you exceed the baseline. For failover we do smart routing — traffic will fall back to a compatible model variant in another region or a quantized variant if available. That said, falling back across region will add latency and potentially cross-region data flow, which is why we let customers set routing policies to avoid cross-region fallbacks for sensitive workloads.
02:48 Evan Torres: That fallback concern is big — we need to disable cross-region fallbacks for the EU accounts. Can we do per-tenant routing?
02:55 Ravi Patel: Yes, per-route and per-tenant policies exist. We can pin EU tenant traffic to eu-west-only and set an automatic fail behavior of queueing or returning a controlled 429 if capacity is exhausted — depends on your tolerance.
03:08 Priya Nandakumar: Queueing could be risky if it impacts SLAs; what are your latency SLO numbers for dedicated vs hosted?
03:16 Ravi Patel: For dedicated with a warm KV cache and steady seq length, 95th percentile generation latency is typically in the low hundreds of milliseconds for short prompts; hosted can be slightly higher due to multi-tenant scheduling — around 20–30% higher on average. We'll share the recent perf deck.
03:31 Maya Chen: Maya interjects: We'll attach the redwood perf deck and the EU region benchmark sheet.
03:36 Jordan Lee: Pricing question — if we go with baseline reserved + burst, how's the billing structured? Flat commit plus burst overage?
03:43 Maya Chen: The typical structure: a monthly reserved commit for Dedicated capacity with a unit price, then burst is billed at hosted rates with a multiplier; we can offer stepped discounts at different commit tiers. For expansion for eu-west we can propose a 12-month term with a tiered pricing schedule that reduces unit cost after hitting usage thresholds.
03:59 Evan Torres: We're also exploring model variants: some of our checkpoints are large, we might test lower-precision quantized variants to reduce cost. Can Redwood handle mixed-precision across routes with transparent routing?
04:12 Ravi Patel: Yes, we can route by model variant and manage quantized profiles. The runtime supports quantized kernels and KV cache compatibility; we track quality metrics so you can get alerted if latency/cost changes correlate with quality regressions.
04:27 Sofia Rivera: About keys and audit — how do you integrate with our AWS KMS in eu-west-1? Any cross-account roles?
04:34 Lina Gomez: We have a pattern: Redwood Private customers can bring their own KMS keys and we support cross-account roles for key wrapping; for Dedicated we can provision per-customer KMS bindings. I'll send the integration checklist and required IAM roles.
04:48 Priya Nandakumar: Is Private deployment required for KMS? We're trying to avoid full private for cost reasons.
04:54 Ravi Patel: Not necessarily. Dedicated plus customer-managed KMS is supported without full Private deployment. Private is primarily for air-gapped or self-hosted control plane scenarios.
05:03 Evan Torres: Okay that helps. On the capacity numbers: currently our peak requires approx 3 A100-equiv GPUs in us-east during highest loads. For EU initial needs we're projecting the equivalent of 4 GPUs to get the tail latency we want. We don't want to commit to 4 year-round. Ideally reserve 2 and allow bursting to 4.
05:22 Maya Chen: Noted. We can propose a 2-reserved / 2-burst config for eu-west with a ramp credit for the first three months while we tune cache and batch configs.
05:31 Jordan Lee: That ramp credit detail sounds useful. Procurement loves credits.
05:33 Priya Nandakumar: On the legal side, we need an SLA addendum. Can Redwood provide 99.9% uptime for Dedicated? What about latency SLOs written in?
05:43 Maya Chen: Our Dedicated SLAs can be 99.9% for availability of reserved pools; latency SLOs are typically operational guarantees with remediation credits but not financial penalties on generation latency. We can add operational metrics and a remediation path to the SOW. We'll involve legal to write an addendum with the specifics.
05:59 Evan Torres: For the pilot, what's the minimum time to provision eu-west nodes?
06:03 Ravi Patel: If we pre-approve capacity, we can spin up dedicated nodes in eu-west within 48–72 hours; otherwise standard provisioning pipeline is about a week. For a pilot we can expedite provisioning if you sign a short-term pilot SOW.
06:17 Sofia Rivera: For the expedited path do you require any network peering or VPC configs from our side?
06:22 Ravi Patel: For Dedicated, we can offer either managed networking (Redwood-managed peering) or VPC peering into your account for private connectivity. The latter needs routing and security groups set up and will require your infra team's involvement.
06:35 Priya Nandakumar: We prefer VPC peering to keep data flows inside our accounts. What about outbound logs — do they go to Redwood account by default?
06:43 Lina Gomez: Defaults can be changed — we can have logs pushed to your S3 buckets in eu-west with proper IAM roles. We'll include that in the checklist.
06:52 Maya Chen: Let's talk timeline — you're up for renewal in early July, correct?
06:56 Priya Nandakumar: Correct. Ideally we'd sign by July 1 to align budgets, but procurement might need two weeks after final SOW.
07:04 Maya Chen: Okay so we have room for a pilot in mid-June to validate latencies and cost. If pilot looks good we can push legal and procurement to close end of June.
07:14 Jordan Lee: That timeline works if we get the SOW + pricing this week.
07:18 Maya Chen: Action item — I'll send an updated pricing + SOW draft by Thursday (2027-06-09).
07:24 Ravi Patel: I'll provision a benchmark environment and run a latency/cost runbook with your sample prompts and traffic shape. I'll need the sample dataset and peak traffic profile.
07:33 Evan Torres: I'll drop the sample prompts and traffic pkls into the shared folder after the call.
07:38 Sofia Rivera: One more security ask — we've had a vendor request to confirm SOC2 attestation plus penetration test cadence. Can you share the latest reports?
07:46 Lina Gomez: Yes — we'll share the SOC2 Type II report under NDA and the pen test summary. I'll include redacted findings and remediation timelines.
07:56 Priya Nandakumar: Good. Also, for the EU region, any data residency certifications or specific GDPR support notes?
08:03 Lina Gomez: We have data residency controls, support for customer-managed keys in-region, and we keep processing localized when you enable EU-only routing. We'll include a GDPR summary doc.
08:16 Evan Torres: On the technical nitpick — when we run quantized variants, how do you ensure prefix KV compatibility if we sometimes switch between full and quantized?
08:24 Ravi Patel: We maintain model-variant compatibility mappings. For straightforward transformer checkpoints the KV cache format is compatible across some quantization levels; when not compatible, we recommend warm-starting the quantized variant or letting the system rebuild caches. We'll capture specifics for your models after the pilot.
08:40 Maya Chen: Great detail. Any other blockers from the customer side before we wrap?
08:45 Jordan Lee: Just procurement needs price and SOW.
08:47 Priya Nandakumar: Exec sponsor wants a 15-minute call with Maya and our CFO before final sign-off — can we schedule that week of June 21?
08:55 Maya Chen: Yes, I'll coordinate. Lina, can you own the SOC2 + pen test docs?
08:59 Lina Gomez: I'll get those uploaded to the secure share by EOD tomorrow.
09:04 Evan Torres: One ask on telemetry — can we get token-level cost reports broken down per-route? That will help us map charges to business units.
09:12 Lina Gomez: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards. I'll include sample screenshots and instructions.
09:20 Ravi Patel: For the benchmark run I will test 95th/99th percentiles and synthetic peak bursts to show tail behavior. I'll also run with quantized variants to give cost deltas.
09:32 Maya Chen: Okay to recap next steps: Maya send pricing + SOW by 2027-06-09; Ravi run pilot benchmarks and deliver report by 2027-06-14; Lina share SOC2 + pen test and GDPR summary by 2027-06-08; Evan to upload prompts and traffic profiles by 2027-06-08; Jordan confirm procurement timeline by 2027-06-11; schedule exec sponsor call week of 2027-06-21.
09:55 Priya Nandakumar: That sounds right, thanks.
09:58 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email and in the shared folder, talk soon.
10:04 (call ends)
